1Outcome

Each participant is supported to understand the terms and conditions that apply to their specialist disability accommodation dwelling and the associated service and/or tenancy agreements.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Work is undertaken with each participant to develop a written service agreement that meets the requirements of the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rules 2018, and any applicable state or territory residential tenancy legislation.

Our commitment: →POL-SDA-03, commitment 1POL-SDA-03 C1→POL-SDA-03, commitment 2POL-SDA-03 C2→POL-SDA-03, commitment 14POL-SDA-03 C14

(2)

In the absence of any applicable state or territory residential tenancy legislation, written service agreements should deal with the following matters:

  1. (a)specify the rent that must be paid by the participant and the method and timing of making rental payments and arrangements for the issuance of rental payment receipts;
  2. (b)specify the value and management arrangements in relation to any bond that is required from the participant;
  3. (c)if applicable, specify any board payments that have been agreed with the participant, what the board payments will cover and the method and timing of making the board payments;
  4. (e)specify the minimum period of notice that will be given by the provider before the provider increases the amount of rent or board (where applicable) payable by the participant;
  5. (f)specify:
    1. (i)the name, telephone number and address of the provider’s agent (if any) and the responsibilities of the agent; or
    2. (ii)if the provider does not have an agent, the address and telephone number, of the provider;
  6. (g)require the provider to notify the participant in writing within 5 business days of any change during the agreement of the matters provided for in paragraph (f), unless applicable state or territory law stipulates an alternative notice period;
  7. (h)specify the commencement date of the agreement, the duration of the agreement, and the manner in which the agreement can be extended;
  8. (j)specify the circumstances in which the agreement can be terminated by either the participant or the provider;
  9. (k)require the provider to give the participant a minimum of 90 days’ notice before the participant is required to vacate the premises, unless shorter notice is required to address risks of harm to the participant or others;
  10. (l)explain the process for requesting repairs or maintenance to be undertaken.

1Purpose

This policy is the frame for every matter at [Provider name]. It names the four thread policies that carry our commitments, and the few rules that bind all of them. It protects the 's rights, their home and their choice of .

2Applies to

  • [Provider name] as a registered NDIS provider of SDA, whether SDA is our only class of supports or one of several.
  • Every we own, lease or manage for SDA, and every dwelling we apply to enrol. This covers every participant who lives in one or is offered a place. A prospective participant has the same rights as a participant (Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 1(2)).
  • Everyone who works at or for a dwelling: employees, contractors, tradespeople, and volunteers.
  • A participant who provides SDA to themselves. The rule in POL-SDA-03 does not apply to them (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(3)). The dwelling rules do.
  • Our own supported independent living in an SDA dwelling. POL-SIL-05, POL-SIL-02, POL-SIL-03 and POL-SUP-03 apply as well.
  • Our two roles, as landlord and as support provider to the same participant. Every commitment applies to both.

3Commitments

Each commitment below points to the thread policy that carries it. The thread policy's numbers, roles and records are the only source of truth; this policy restates none of them.

C1

We will do what POL-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: each participant's rights at home, their privacy, and every request to change their dwelling.

C2

We will do what the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) commits to, applied to SDA through PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation): every interest we hold is declared, and a participant's home never depends on their choice of supports.

C3

We will do what POL-SDA-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: a written agreement with every participant, in the terms the law requires.

C4

We will do what POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of SDA Properties Policy commits to: kept within their enrolment, lawful, safe and in good repair.

C5

We will do what POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: fair vacancies, documented arrangements with each SIL provider, and tenancy notices that follow the law.

4Ground rules

The thread policies carry their own ground rules. These four are the ones no thread policy carries, and they bind every SDA procedure.

G1

Every participant has a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share one (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(d)). A participant who chooses to share must tell the in writing, and the NDIA must be satisfied that their needs are not harmed; a notice alone is not the end of it. We help them do it (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(e)).

G2

Where we own or manage the dwelling, we lead on the dwelling, its repairs and its vacancies. A SIL provider leads on the supports it delivers. Where a matter involves both, the arrangement under AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement names one lead, and both act together.

G3

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader names an for concerns in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, with a written delegation that covers every task the thread policies and procedures give that person. The independent contact is not a relative or business associate of the sole trader, has access to REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register, REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register and the register (REG-GOV-02), and is briefed on PRO-SDA-03 and PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) before acting.

G4

If we will miss a time we promised a participant, we tell them before it passes, with the reason and the new date. A time the law sets cannot be moved.

9Words we use

567 words
SDA agreement
the written agreement between us and a participant about their home.
dwelling
a home in which we provide SDA. An enrolled dwelling is one the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it.
participant
a person with disability who lives in a dwelling, or is offered a place in one.
tenant
a person who lives in a dwelling and has a right to be there.
eligible participant
a participant the NDIA has decided is eligible for SDA funding (SDA Rules 2020, section 11).
other supports
every NDIS support a participant gets apart from the home, from us or from anyone else. Examples are SIL, support coordination and plan management.
supported independent living (SIL)
help with, or supervision of, daily tasks so a person can live as independently as possible.
design category and building type
the features the NDIA enrolled a dwelling under. The SDA Rules 2020 set five design categories and four building types.
density limit
a cap on how many eligible participants can be funded for SDA across every dwelling on one parcel of land (SDA Rules 2020, section 31).
conflict of interest
a clash between what we, a worker or someone close to us gains and what is best for the participant. It is actual when it affects a decision, potential when it could, and perceived when it looks as if it could.
security of tenure
a participant's right to keep living in their home unless the SDA agreement and tenancy law allow it to end.
tenancy law
the law of [state or territory] about renting a home, including notices, bonds and entry.
notice to vacate
a written notice that tells a participant they must leave their home.
tenancy action
a notice to vacate, a breach notice, any rent or board increase, a room move, or a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant.
tenure check
the Chief Executive's decision, before a tenancy action is served, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or worries.
modification
a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate.
urgent defect
a fault that puts anyone at risk of harm, or stops a participant washing, using the toilet, preparing food, sleeping or leaving home. Examples: no water or power, a gas or electrical fault, a broken lock or door, a failed lift, hoist or fire alarm, a blocked exit.
independent advocate
a person who is not part of [Provider name], chosen by the participant, who speaks up for their wishes and rights. An advocate does not make decisions for them.
independent contact
in a small provider, a person outside our management, named in REG-GOV-01, who acts when the Chief Executive has an interest.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency. The SDA Rules 2020 give its notices to its CEO.
NDIS Commission
the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.
SDA Manager
the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
Tenancy Officer
the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule, Practice Standards Rules, Complaints Rules, Incident Rules, Quality Indicators
short names for the instruments in Authority.

1Purpose

The result: every in one of our has a written they helped to shape and understood. They hold a signed copy of it. The money, the notice periods, the repairs and the safety information are written in it. Every change and every ending follows it.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation), C1 to C15.

2When and who

Start this procedure at the step that matches what has happened:

  • A participant has accepted a place in one of our dwellings, or we find a participant living in one with no agreement: start at step 1.
  • A safety feature or the way out of the building changes: step 21.
  • Our , our address or our telephone number changes: step 22.
  • or is going up: step 23.
  • The agreement is due for review, the participant asks to see or change it, or a fixed term is near its end: step 24.
  • We think we may need to end an agreement: step 25. Steps 25 to 27 prepare the notice. PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) steps 24 to 27 serve it.
  • A participant gives us notice that they are leaving: PRO-SDA-05 step 28 ends the tenancy. Then do step 28 here.

Who acts:

  • The prepares the agreement, explains it, gives the copy and keeps the records.
  • The checks every draft, decides changes, signs for us, tells the and decides whether we may end an agreement.
  • The Chief Executive decides whether to charge rent above the limit and approves every notice to end an agreement.
  • The Quality Manager samples the records every 3 months.
  • Every worker tells the Tenancy Officer within 1 when a participant asks about, or wants to change, their agreement.

If an agent does the Tenancy Officer's work, the agent follows this procedure. [Provider name] stays responsible, and the SDA Manager checks the agent's work at step 10.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader still needs a second person for steps 6, 10, 25 (the at PRO-SDA-03 step 23) and 26, and for the approval of any notice to end an agreement at PRO-SDA-05 step 24. REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names that person as [independent contact for concerns].

A business day is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. The SDA Manager is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The Tenancy Officer is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. The agreement is the completed AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement for one participant and one dwelling, with every change. A is an agreement we have worked out with the participant and given them a copy of, before they have signed it.

Short names used here:

  • SDA Rules 2020: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020
  • SDA Conditions Rule: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018
  • NDIA: the National Disability Insurance Agency
  • : the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission

3Before you start

  • You have the current AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement. Use the template itself. Do not start from an old signed copy.
  • You can open REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register, REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register and REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.
  • You have the dwelling's latest FRM-SDA-03 SDA Dwelling Inspection and Compliance Checklist.
  • You have the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, or you will complete one at step 2.
  • You have STA-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement: Plain Summary in the participant's format.
  • You know how PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) and PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure fit with this one. PRO-SDA-05 opens the tenancy row, serves notices and ends tenancies. PRO-SDA-01 deals with repairs.
  • You know these contacts: [repair contact], [urgent number], [advocacy service] and [tenancy advice service]. You know the NDIS Commission number, 1800 035 544.
  • You have done PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) steps 5 to 8 with this participant, or you will do them before step 11.
  • REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows you have done the training for this procedure under PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure.

Law changing: from 20 November 2026 the NDIS Act 2013 bans inducements to provide supports (new section 73VA, inserted by the NDIS Amendment (Securing the NDIS for Future Generations) Act 2026, Schedule 2 Part 8; the Department publishes 27 November 2026, so confirm the day). PRO-SDA-03 step 4 and step 11 of this procedure already bar any gift, discount or other benefit tied to a participant's choice.

4Watch out

  • Danger comes first. If anyone is in danger, call 000 before you do anything else on this page. A repair or a form can wait. A person in danger cannot.
  • No agreement, no stay. Providing SDA with no signed agreement, and no proposed agreement in the participant's hands, breaks a condition of registration (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1)). A civil penalty can follow (NDIS Act 2013, section 73J).
  • A signature is not understanding. A participant who signs without understanding can lose rights they did not know they had. Step 13 asks them to say or show it back.
  • A carer cannot sign for an adult. A family member or carer with no legal authority cannot sign for a participant. An agreement they sign may not hold, and the participant is left without one.
  • Rent above the limit. Charging rent above the limit without telling the NDIA breaks a condition of enrolment. The NDIA can cancel the dwelling's enrolment (SDA Rules 2020, section 27).
  • Fewer than 90 days. Shorter notice can leave a participant with nowhere to go. Only the Chief Executive can approve it, in writing, and only for a .
  • A notice after a support choice. A notice soon after a participant changes support provider looks like punishment. Step 25 needs the tenure check first.
  • Missing safety information. A provider who does not know the exits and the alarms may not get the participant out in a fire. PRO-SDA-05 step 14 gives it to a new provider before their first shift. Step 21 sends any change.
  • The 5 business days to tell the NDIA. The time is set by law. PRO-SDA-05 step 2 tells the NDIA. Missing the time breaks a condition of enrolment.

Result

  • if the participant has not signed, they hold the proposed agreement and we provide their home under its terms
  • every question in Sections A to I of AGR-SDA-01 has an answer
  • the safety information is with every provider who delivers supported independent living in the dwelling
  • the agreement is entered in REG-SDA-02.

These records now exist:

  • the completed AGR-SDA-01 in the participant's file, with its dated versions

1What this agreement is for

This is the written between [Provider name] and a about the participant's . It sets out the and other money, how long the agreement lasts and how it can end. It also sets out how repairs work, and the rights and responsibilities of both of us. It is the written service agreement that the SDA Conditions Rule, section 9, requires. The SDA Rules 2020, section 36, require it too. The SDA Conditions Rule is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018. The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020.

In this agreement "you" is the participant and "we" is [Provider name]. The completes the Schedule with you, in the way you choose to communicate. You can take your time, bring a person you trust, and ask for changes. STA-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement: Plain Summary says the same things in fewer words.

This agreement is about your home only. If we also give you supports, we do that under a separate agreement, AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template. PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) sets every step. A copy signed by both of us is yours to keep. Records go to REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register.

2Terms

About this agreement

T1

"You" is the participant named in Schedule Q1 and "we" is [Provider name], ABN [ABN]. A is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where you live.

T2

This agreement is about your right to live in the dwelling named in Schedule Q2. It is not about your supports. If we also give you supports, we do that under a separate agreement.

T3

If the law of [state or territory] requires a tenancy agreement on a prescribed form, we sign it with you as well. Schedule Q4 names it.

T4

This agreement never takes away a right the law gives you. If the law gives you more than this agreement, you have what the law gives. If this agreement gives you more than the law, you have what this agreement gives.

Your home and your supports

T5

Your home does not depend on who gives you supports. You can choose, change or stop any support provider, including one we work with, and you keep your home.

T6

We will not ask you to buy a support or service from us, or from a person we name, as a condition of this agreement.

T7

Before you sign, we tell you about every interest we have in your home or your supports. An example is owning your home and also giving you supports. We give you our policy at least 3 business days before we ask you to sign, unless you ask us, in your own words, for less time.

T8

Other NDIS providers can come into your dwelling to give you supports. We will not restrict them.

T9

We will not use a choice you make about your own life, including a choice that carries risk, as a reason to end this agreement.

Our responsibilities for your dwelling

T10

We will keep your dwelling in a good state of repair and properly maintained, with care for your safety, security and privacy.

T11

We will keep your dwelling as it was enrolled for SDA. We will not house more residents in it than the number in Schedule Q2.

T12

We pay for the repair and upkeep of the dwelling and its fittings. We pay to connect the water, power and other utilities. You pay only for the water, power or internet you use, and only if Schedule Q14 says so and how it is worked out.

T13

You pay for damage only if you cause it and it is more than fair wear and tear. Before we ask you to pay, we check whether a missing support or adjustment caused it. If it did, we fix that first and do not charge you. We show you the evidence in writing, and you can dispute it.

T14

We enter your dwelling only for a reason this agreement or the law allows: an inspection, a repair or work, a check on the safety features, or to show the dwelling to a person who may move in, a valuer or a buyer. We give you notice in your way of communicating that says who is coming, why, the day, the time window and which rooms. The notice is at least 7 days for an inspection, a check or planned work, and at least 2 business days for a repair you asked for, or longer where the law of [state or territory] gives you more. You can agree to less. We go into your bedroom only with your agreement, each time. We never use a key to come in while you are home, except in an emergency. We enter without notice only in an emergency, to keep someone safe or to protect the dwelling, and we tell you why within 24 hours.

T15

House rules, if there are any, are agreed with the people who live in the dwelling and written down. We give you a copy in your way of communicating and review them with the residents once a year. They never limit your rights under this agreement or the law.

Rent and other money

T16

You pay the rent in Schedule Q7. The SDA amount in your plan is funded under the NDIS, and you do not pay that part. We show you how we worked out your rent.

T17

We will not charge rent above the limit the NDIS rules set for SDA without first telling the National Disability Insurance Agency (). We give the NDIA a valuer's certificate that the rent is fair and reasonable. We tell you as well.

T18

You pay rent in the way and on the days you chose in Schedule Q9. We offer at least two ways to pay. You can change your way or your day by telling us, and we confirm the change in writing within 5 business days.

T19

We give you a receipt at the time for a cash payment. For other payments we give you a receipt or a statement, in the format you chose in Schedule Q10, every [set at adoption], and at any time you ask.

T20

Your is the amount in Schedule Q11, which may be nothing. We never ask for more than the law of [state or territory] allows.

T21

We look after your bond as Schedule Q12 says. Where the law requires, we lodge it with the authority it names, within the time it sets.

T22

We return your bond within the days in Schedule Q12 after you leave. We keep back an amount only for unpaid rent, or for damage you caused beyond fair wear and tear. We show you the evidence in writing first, and tell you how to dispute it.

T23

You pay only if you chose it in Schedule Q13, and it covers only what Q13 lists. If you are away for longer than the days in Q13, we reduce board for the days you are away. You can ask for a statement of what board paid for, and we give it within 10 business days.

T24

We charge you nothing that is not written in Schedule Q7 to Q14. We charge no fee for signing this agreement, moving in, changing the agreement or ending it.

T25

We give you written notice before we increase your rent or board. The notice is at least the longer of 60 days and what the law of [state or territory] requires, and never less than the days in Schedule Q15.

T26

If the limit on your rent goes down, we lower your rent from the day the limit goes down. If your SDA funding changes or stops, or your plan's design category changes, we tell you within 5 business days of learning of it and help you seek a review. Your rent does not change for at least 60 days, and then only by written notice under term 25. We do not end this agreement for that reason alone for at least 90 days, and we work with you and the supporters you choose on what happens next.

Who you deal with

T27

Schedule Q16 names our , if we have one, with the agent's telephone number, address and responsibilities. Schedule Q17 gives our address and telephone number.

T28

We stay responsible for everything in this agreement, including work done by our agent.

T29

We tell you in writing within 5 business days if our address or telephone number changes. We do the same if our agent, or the agent's address, number or responsibilities, change. If the law of [state or territory] sets a different period, we use that period.

How long this agreement lasts

T30

This agreement starts on the date in Schedule Q18 and lasts for the time in Schedule Q19.

T31

A fixed term continues on the same terms after its end date, unless it ends under terms 34 to 45. At least 90 days before the end date we write to you to confirm that it continues. Your home does not end because a term ends.

T32

We review this agreement with you at least every 12 months, and whenever you ask or something important changes. Schedule Q21 gives the first review date.

T33

We change this agreement only in writing, and only with your agreement. The exceptions are a change the law requires and the notices in terms 25 and 29. We give you a copy of every change.

Ending this agreement

T34

You can end this agreement at any time. You give us notice, in writing or in the way you communicate, of the days in Schedule Q22. We accept shorter notice if you ask.

T35

You and we can end this agreement at any time by agreeing to it in writing.

T36

We can end this agreement only for a reason in term 37, and only by following this agreement and the law of [state or territory]. If the law lets us use another reason, we do not use it.

T37

The reasons we can use are:

  • you have not paid rent, and we have done what term 38 says
  • you have seriously or repeatedly broken a responsibility in this agreement, and we have done what term 38 says
  • your behaviour puts you or someone else at risk of serious harm, and no other way of reducing the risk has worked
  • the dwelling cannot be lived in, will be sold, or will stop being used for SDA; we have looked for and, where we can, offered you another suitable home, and you choose whether to accept it
  • your needs have changed beyond what the dwelling can meet, even after the adjustments and we can reasonably make
  • you have not been at the dwelling and we cannot reach you for [set at adoption] days (the period the law of [state or territory] sets for abandoned premises, where it sets one), after we have checked on your welfare.
T38

Before we give notice for unpaid rent or a broken responsibility, we do four things. We talk with you and the people you choose. We tell you in writing what the problem is and what would fix it. We offer help, such as an advocate, a payment arrangement or an adjustment. We give you at least 14 days to fix it, and longer where the law says.

T39

We give you at least 90 days' written notice before you must leave the dwelling, and longer where the law of [state or territory] says. We use only a reason in term 37 that the law of [state or territory] allows.

T40

We give shorter notice only where it is needed to address a to you or to someone else. We do this only where the law allows it. Our Chief Executive decides in writing first, names the risk, and says why 90 days would not keep people safe. We tell you the reason in the way you communicate.

T41

We never end this agreement because:

  • you chose or changed your support provider, including your SIL provider
  • you made a complaint
  • you asked for a repair, a change to your home, or your rights
  • you took advice from an advocate
  • you did not sign an arrangement with us and your SIL provider, or did not sign this agreement
  • someone else wants your home.
T42

Every notice from us tells you in writing how to ask for it to be looked at again. This includes our complaints process, the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission (the ), and the tribunal or other body of [state or territory] that deals with tenancies.

T43

We tell the NDIA within 5 business days when you or we give notice to end this agreement.

T44

If notice is given, we help you find another safe place to live. We work with the supporters and providers you choose, and we share your information only with your consent.

T45

If you die, this agreement ends on the day the law of [state or territory] says or, where no applies, 28 days after we are told. No rent is charged after that day. We release your belongings to your executor or next of kin, and we deal with your bond as the law requires, with respect for you and for the people close to you.

T46

When this agreement ends, we do a final check of the dwelling with you. We return your bond as in term 22, and we give you a final statement of your rent. Anything you leave behind is kept safe and returned to you, or to your executor, as the law of [state or territory] requires.

Repairs and maintenance

T47

You can ask for a repair or for maintenance in any way you choose. You can tell a worker, phone, write, send a message, or ask a supporter to ask for you. Schedule Q24 gives our repair contact and our urgent number.

T48

We acknowledge every repair request by the next business day. We tell you who will deal with it and how we have rated it.

T49

A repair is an emergency if someone's life or health is at immediate risk, such as a failed ventilator power supply or a gas leak: call 000 first, your medical emergency plan applies, and we act the same day. A repair is urgent if your safety or security is at risk now, or if you cannot use your bedroom, bathroom, toilet, kitchen or way in and out. Examples are a smoke alarm that does not work, a gas smell, a lock that does not work, no water or power, or a lift, hoist or door opener you rely on that is out of use. We make an urgent repair safe within 24 hours, and the same day where your safety or a life-support device depends on it, or we agree another safe way for you to use the room or feature. We finish it within 2 business days. If anyone is in danger, call 000 first.

T50

A repair is high if it lowers your safety, security or privacy, or something does not work but you can still use your home. Examples are a leak, a bedroom door that will not close, or a broken heater. We put a temporary measure in place within 1 business day. We finish a high repair, and any other repair that is not planned works, within 5 business days of your request, or sooner where the law of [state or territory] requires.

T51

A repair is planned works if it needs approvals, the owner's work, or a long wait for parts. We tell you the date within 5 business days and keep a temporary measure in place for the whole wait. You must agree to any date more than 14 days away. If we cannot meet any date, we tell you before it passes, give the reason and set a new date.

T52

If you think a repair is not being dealt with, you can complain to us. You can also take the matter to the tribunal or other body of [state or territory] that deals with tenancies. Where tenancy law sets a shorter time for a repair, that time applies. Where the law lets you arrange an urgent repair and be repaid, you keep that right.

Safety in your home

T53

Schedule Q25 lists the safety features of your dwelling, including smoke alarms and other fire alarms. Schedule Q26 sets out how you get out of the building in a fire or other emergency.

T54

We explain the safety features and the way out to you before you move in, in the way you communicate. We practise leaving the building with you within 5 business days of your move, and again after any change to them.

T55

We keep the safety features working, and check them as often as the law and building standards require. You tell us straight away if one does not work.

T56

We give the safety features and the way out to each provider who delivers supported independent living to you in the dwelling. We give it in writing, and we walk the provider's nominated person through the dwelling before the provider's first shift, and the provider briefs its own workers. We do it again within 5 business days of any change. Schedule Q27 lists the providers. We share information about your own needs only with your consent.

T57

If a fire, flood or other emergency makes your dwelling unsafe, we tell you the same day what we are doing and who is helping. We work with your SIL provider and the NDIA to find you a safe place that meets your needs as soon as possible, and within 24 hours. You keep your tenancy, and you pay no rent for any time you cannot live in the dwelling.

Your rights

T58

We treat you with respect and dignity. We respect your privacy, your culture, your relationships and your right to make your own decisions.

T59

You can have visitors and relationships in your home, and your privacy and intimacy are respected. We set no rule about visitors that is not in this agreement or the law. You can ask us to add or change a lock under term 61; we hold a sealed emergency key, used only in an emergency and recorded each time. An assistance animal lives with you as the law allows.

T60

You can have a supporter, an advocate or a person you trust with you for anything to do with this agreement. We help you contact an advocate if you ask.

T61

You can ask for a change to your dwelling, or to how we manage it. We acknowledge your request within 2 business days, and we decide within 20 business days and tell you why.

T62

You can raise a concern or complaint with us in any way. We deal with it under our complaints process, and it never puts your home at risk. Our complaints contact is [complaints contact]. You can also contact the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544, [advocacy service] or [tenancy advice service].

T63

We keep your information private. We share it only with your consent, or where the law requires it. You can ask to see it and to correct it.

Your responsibilities

T64

You pay your rent and any other charge in this agreement on time. If you cannot, tell us early. We will talk with you and agree a payment arrangement before we take any other step.

T65

You look after your dwelling and its fittings. You tell us about damage and about repairs that are needed.

T66

You let us in when we have given you the notice in term 14, or in an emergency.

T67

You respect the rights of the people who live with you and near you.

T68

You do not cover, disable or remove a smoke alarm, and you do not block an exit.

T69

You tell us about a change that affects this agreement. Examples are a change to your rent assistance, income support or plan, or a long absence. We ask only for what we need.

Understanding, signing and your copy

T70

We explain this agreement in the language, mode of communication and terms you are most likely to understand. We arrange and pay for an interpreter or a communication partner if you want one.

T71

We give you at least 5 business days to think about this agreement before you sign. You can sign sooner if you choose to. You can take it away and show a person you trust.

T72

We never ask you to sign a blank or unfinished agreement.

T73

We check that you understand the main terms by asking you to tell us or show us in your own way. If you do not yet, we explain again. Your signature alone does not show that you understand.

T74

You sign for yourself. A guardian, nominee, attorney or other person signs for you only with legal authority that covers this agreement. We ask to see it. A family member or carer with no legal authority cannot sign for you. We still involve you in every decision.

T75

If you have not signed, we give you a copy of the and we provide your home under its terms. We keep working with you on it. Not signing is not a reason to end this agreement.

T76

We give you a copy signed by you and by us within 2 business days of the last signature. If we cannot, we write down why within the same 2 business days. We offer you the copy again within 5 business days, and at each review, until you have it.

T77

We keep this agreement and every change for 7 years after it ends (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B).

+Privacy

This part is not one the anatomy names for this kind of document.

We collect the information in this agreement and its Schedule to set up and manage your home, to meet the SDA Conditions Rule, the SDA Rules 2020 and the NDIS Practice Standards, and to show that you understood and agreed.

The Tenancy Officer, the and the Chief Executive read it, and our agent where we have one. In REG-SDA-02 we write your participant number, never your name, beside the facts of your tenancy. An auditor or the NDIS Commission may see it as the law allows. We give your SIL providers only the dwelling's safety information, and information about your own needs only with your consent on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form.

You can see this agreement and its Schedule at any time and ask us to correct anything in it. Ask any worker, or use FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form. Asking never puts your home at risk. We keep this agreement and every change for 7 years after it ends (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B). POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] looks after each . It shows how we enrol it, keep it inside its enrolment, and keep it safe, secure, private and in good repair. Each row is one record about one dwelling. A row shows what was found or decided, who did it, which residents were told, and when the next action falls due.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 71 (1), s 71 (2) and s 71 (3).
  • The columns also evidence s 68 (1) and s 72 (5). FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and Adjustment Request sends its rows here.
  • Legal basis: Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 6. SDA Conditions Rule, sections 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. SDA Rules 2020, sections 5 to 8, 15, 19 and 24 to 32.
  • The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. The SDA Conditions Rule is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • No law sets the columns of this register. They are our standard, built from what the law makes us certify, notify and keep.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded. Keep a dwelling row for 7 years after the dwelling stops being enrolled with us (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years; this register's rows support SDA claims, so 7 years is also the statutory floor.
  • Other law can require a certificate or a safety record to be kept longer. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.
  • Roles and words: : the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. : the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the lives. List of laws: the dated list of state and territory laws kept once in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.

The register holds ten types of row. Column C names the type. Columns A to Q are the spine, and every row uses them. Each type then fills its own group of columns:

  • dwelling: columns R to AE
  • limits check: columns AF to AH
  • certificate or service: columns AI to AK
  • inspection: columns AL to AT
  • repair: columns AU to BA
  • modification record: columns BB to BG and BP to BT
  • entry record: column BH
  • matter: columns BI to BK
  • compliance check: columns BL to BM
  • house rules check: columns BN to BO

Residents' names are not kept here. A row uses resident numbers. A resident number is the number we use in place of a name, for example the participant's record number in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Register. Health details, behaviour support content and a resident's own words stay on their own file.

Keep each row type on its own sheet, with the spine columns first. A provider with one dwelling has few rows: one dwelling row, two inspections a year, and a handful of certificate or service rows.
register.entry:
1. The SDA Manager adds every row. The Tenancy Officer adds entry records and modification records, and may add a repair row from a resident's report. The Quality Manager adds compliance check rows, and inspection rows for a sample re-inspection. The person who enters a home records the entry the same day, and the Tenancy Officer adds the entry record. When the SDA Manager is away, the Tenancy Officer adds rows.
  2. Add the row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Add an NDIA matter row, a repair row and its rating within 1 business day, and an emergency or urgent repair row the same day.
  3. Use one row for each limits check, certificate or service due, inspection, defect, modification request, entry and NDIA matter. An inspection that finds 3 defects makes 4 rows, plus a limits check row. Link them at col P.
  4. A dwelling has one dwelling row in force at a time. When a dwelling fact changes, add a new version of the row with the date, your name and the reason. The old version becomes "superseded".
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Write resident numbers, not names. Leave out health details, behaviour support content and a resident's private words.
  7. Use one row each time a certificate or a service falls due. When it is done, close the row and open the next one.
  8. When someone was hurt or nearly hurt, the event is also an incident. Write its number from REG-INC-01 Incident Register at col P. A complaint goes in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. A hazard to people while supports are given goes in REG-ENV-01 Hazard and Maintenance Register. Tenancy facts go in REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register. Link each one here.
  9. At any time, each must show a dwelling row with the status "enrolled". It must show an inspection row and a limits check row, each not older than 6 months. Its certificate or service rows must not be past their due dates, and no repair row may be past its due date.
  10. Reopen a closed row when the defect comes back. Set col N to "reopened" and write the reason.

Modification recordEach change a participant asks for, sent here from FRM-SDA-01A to Q, BB to BG, BP to BT

A row is closed only when all of these are true for its type:

  • Dwelling: a new version has replaced it, or the dwelling is no longer enrolled with us and the NDIA has been told.
  • Limits check: the result is recorded. If it was "over a limit", the Chief Executive has decided what happens.
  • Certificate or service: the certificate or report is filed, and the next one has its own row.
  • Inspection: every defect has its own row, each resident has been told the result, and the next inspection date is set.
  • Repair: the work is done, someone other than the contractor has checked it, the resident says it is fixed, and the resident has been told. Any NDIA matter row for it is also closed.
  • Modification record: FRM-SDA-01 question 37 is answered.
  • Entry record: the visit is recorded, with the time out and any key used.
  • NDIA matter: the notice or answer was sent, proof is filed, and the NDIA's reply is recorded. A notice we sent may close on "no reply" after 20 business days (our standard). An application for enrolment, a request from the NDIA and a notice from the NDIA stay open until the NDIA decides.
  • Compliance check: every change found has an owner and a due date.
  • House rules check: every limit found is removed, or has its lawful authority and the Chief Executive's decision on file. Each resident affected has been told.

The SDA Manager approves closing. The Quality Manager approves closing for an urgent repair row, an NDIA matter row and a dwelling row.

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] manages each tenancy in its . Each row is one record. It shows what was done, who took part, what the said and chose, and who checked.

It holds nine kinds of record: tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, notice rule, notice, change, home event, concern and review. An arrangement is the with the participant's . A concern is anything raised about a dwelling that is not yet a complaint, a repair or an incident.

Complaints, incidents and repairs are not copied here. They stay in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register, REG-INC-01 Incident Register and REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register. A row here links to them in column O.

In this register:

  • "SDA Conditions Rule" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • "SDA Rules 2020" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020.
  • "Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "Complaints Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Complaints Management and Resolution) Rules 2018.
  • "Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
  • "" means the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. "" means the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. "" means a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
  • Indicators evidenced: s 72 (1) to (5), (8) and (9), including s 72 (3)(a) to (3)(h). Columns O and BL link to the complaints and incident records that evidence s 72 (6) and (7); those indicators are proved by the complaints and incident systems, not here. A SIL provider that signs an arrangement can use its arrangement row for Module 5A, sections 72A to 72E (from 1 July 2026).
  • Legal basis: NDIS Act 2013, section 73F(2)(a) and (c). It makes compliance with the law and the NDIS Practice Standards a condition of registration. The SDA Conditions Rule (sections 6 and 8 to 11) and the SDA Rules 2020 (sections 24, 29 and 32) set duties; section 37 of the SDA Rules 2020 is the equivalent of Conditions Rule section 10(2)(b) for registered providers of supports. This register evidences them. No NDIS rule sets the columns. They are our standard, built from the indicators and those duties.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years, so 7 years is also the statutory floor. An incident or complaint record has its own limit. It is 7 years from the day it is made (statutory: Incident Rules, section 12(4); Complaints Rules, section 10(3)).
  • Other law can require longer, for example about . Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.

Which columns apply:

  • Every row fills columns A to O. These are the spine.
  • A tenancy row also fills columns P to W.
  • An arrangement row also fills columns X to AH. Every tenancy has an arrangement row. Where no SIL provider delivers supports in the dwelling to the participant, the row says so and sets a date to check again.
  • A vacancy row also fills columns AI to AT.
  • A notice rule row fills columns AU and AV.
  • A notice row also fills columns AW to BE.
  • A change row also fills columns BF to BH.
  • A home event row also fills columns BI to BN.
  • A review row also fills column BO.
  • A concern row also fills columns BP to BS.
register.entry:
1. The SDA Manager owns the register and approves the closing of every row. The Tenancy Officer adds tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, change and concern rows. The SDA Manager adds notice rows, notice rule rows, home event rows and monthly review rows. The Tenancy Officer completes the service and review rights columns of a notice row, and opens a notice row for a participant's own notice. The Quality Manager adds the 3-monthly and 12-monthly review rows.
  2. Add a row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Five rows are faster. Open a vacancy row within 1 business day of learning of the vacancy. Open a home event row within 1 business day. Open a concern row within 1 business day, when the concern is acknowledged. Open a notice rule row before the first notice of that kind. Enter a notice row before the notice is served.
  3. Use one row for each event. Where a record concerns several residents, columns AM, AO and AP hold one dated line for each person.
  4. Name participants by participant number. Name applicants by applicant number only. Never write an applicant's name in this register.
  5. Keep health details, diagnoses and behaviour support plan content out of the register. Put them on the participant's own file and give the file reference in column N.
  6. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  7. A new SIL provider, or a change to who is responsible for a matter, is a new arrangement row. Set the old row to "superseded" on the same day.
  8. Nobody enters or approves a row about their own decision. The second approver in column AX is never the person who decided.
  9. When systems are down, write the record on paper. Enter the row within 2 business days of the system coming back.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • every column required for its record type is filled
  • each action in column J is done, or sits in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date
  • the participant was told the outcome, and column K shows the date and way
  • the SDA Manager has approved closing.

A tenancy row stays "current" until column W is filled. An arrangement row stays "current" until a new row supersedes it. A vacancy row closes when column AT is filled, or when the SDA Manager records that the place is withdrawn. A notice rule row stays "current" until the law changes and a new row supersedes it. A notice row closes when column BE shows the result. A change row closes when column BG or column BH is filled and the participant was told. A home event row closes when the action in column BM is done, or is tracked in REG-QMS-01. A concern row closes when column BR is filled and column BS shows where it went and how the person was told.

These are trends:

  • a vacancy open for more than 30 days: the SDA Manager reviews the advertising and the criteria within 5 business days
  • two notices to vacate at one dwelling in 12 months: the Chief Executive reviews them within 10 business days
  • any notice to vacate within 6 months of the participant raising a concern or making a complaint: the Chief Executive reviews it within 10 business days
  • three conflicts at one dwelling in 4 weeks: the SDA Manager reviews the house rules and shared spaces with the residents within 10 business days
  • a tenancy with no arrangement row 10 business days after we learn who the SIL provider is: the Chief Executive is told the same day.

Each review is a review row in column BO. The register shows the date of the last review of each kind at the top. A review that leaves no dated row did not happen.

A workbook (.xlsx) generated from this column guide is supplied with the 0.3.0 set, with a Register sheet of the column headers and a Column guide sheet; at adoption it is completed with one sheet per record type, drop-down lists for the allowed values, the calculated days at columns AJ, AT, AZ and BS, and the trends above as conditional formatting.
